title: Putting the rise of the Inca Empire within a climatic and land management context
source_family: Marcacocha palaeoecological core; independent of HYDE, related to earlier Chepstow-Lusty reconstructions
source_locators: Study location, printed p.376 / PDF p.2
observations: Rare maize pollen and chenopod recovery accompany agricultural return in AD1100-1400
Agricultural clearance and possible terrace construction around AD1170
Site water access includes perennial glacial-fed Patacancha River
limitations: Core represents Marcacocha catchment, not measured fields or yields across every Cusco location
Some proxy material is missing for approximately AD1320-1400 following radiocarbon sampling
Possible terrace construction is an interpretation, not a mapped hectare estimate
Current potato cultivation does not by itself date potato use to1337
No later imperial land expansion may be backdated
model_action: Pending explicit geographical crosswalk and crop-presence review; no capacity, development, yield or land assignment changed from this record
status: source recorded; not yet a calibrated crop assignment
